10-15X. MOS 15X—Tactical Unmanned Aircraft System (TUAS) Specialist, CMF 15 (Effective
202610)
     a. Major duties. The TUAS Specialist employs, operates, trains, repairs, services, modifies,
fabricates, and inspects unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) and associated ground equipment for UAS
groups one through three at brigade and below. Integrates into maneuver formations to conduct, assist,
and train UAS operations in contact. Performs planning, analysis, and execution of aerial reconnaissance
and tailors lethal and non-lethal UAS payloads to fit the mission's targeting objectives. Conducts site
selection, emplacement, cover, concealment, and deployment of aircraft and ground equipment. Performs
pre-flight, in-flight, and post-flight checks and procedures. Executes launch/recovery ground crew
operations. Exercises electromagnetic spectrum discipline and adjusts UAS control and video frequencies
to counter electronic warfare threats. Duties for MOS 15X at each level of skill are:
       (1) MOSC 15X1O. Executes UAS reconnaissance, security, target acquisition, and attack missions.
Plans and analyzes flight missions. Designs, fabricates, configures, and tests UAS and associated
payloads, ground control stations, and communication systems. Prepares UAS for deployment, shipment,
and storage. Launches, controls, and recovers aircraft, performing pre-flight, in-flight, and post-flight
inspections and operational checks. Conducts scheduled and unscheduled maintenance on airframes,
payloads, and ground support equipment. Manages fuel, battery, and munitions systems, including
transport, storage, and recovery. Operates mission planning systems, flight simulators, and tactical
communication networks. Troubleshoots and repairs electrical components, flight controllers, and radio
frequency systems using diagnostic tools. Maintains technical records and participates in site setup,
breakdown, and after-action reviews. Ensures proper handling of hazardous materials and compliance
with operational safety standards.
       (2) MOSC 15X2O. Performs duties shown in preceding skill levels and provides guidance to
subordinate Soldiers. Integrates emerging UAS capabilities and assists development of the operator and
gunnery training program. Executes training of UAS Operators across formations on UAS assembly,
operation, employment, and gunnery. Supervises and assists site setup and breakdown. Participates in
mission planning including terrain, threat, and current situation analysis. Participates in and supervises
operator maintenance and crew procedures performed on UAS air and ground equipment. Serves as the
primary trainer of TUAS Specialists as a unit trainer. Monitors proper handling and storage of flammable,
explosive, and hazardous materials. Schedules maintenance on test, measurement and diagnostic
equipment (TMDE).
       (3) MOSC 15X3O. Performs duties shown in preceding skill levels and provides guidance to
subordinate Soldiers. Advises commanders on optimal UAS integration and employment techniques,
tactics, and procedures to include payload capability, payload employment, airspace management, and
electromagnetic spectrum survivability. Manages the UAS training, gunnery, standardization and safety
programs. Synchronizes UAS frequency management against threat EW. Performs, supervises, and
provides technical guidance to subordinate personnel performing UAS operations, maintenance, and
crew procedures. Performs site selection using maps, photographs, terrain analysis, and information
reports. Evaluates maintenance operations and facilities for compliance with directives, technical
manuals, work standards, safety procedures and operational policies. Performs technical inspections.
Applies production control, quality control and other maintenance management principles and
procedures. Computes basic weight and balance and ensures compliance with aircraft configuration
control, Army Oil Analysis Program, and TMDE calibration. Supervises site setup and breakdown.
Coordinates with adjacent, higher, and supported units. Conducts pre-combat checks and inspections.
Supervises the conduct of after-action reviews (AAR). Monitors requisition of parts, tools and supplies.
       (4) MOSC 15X4O. Performs duties shown in preceding skill levels and provides guidance to
subordinate Soldiers. Supervises operations and activities of the platoon. Applies military intelligence
collection, targeting processes, and security planning to UAS operations. Conducts and assists
development of the unit training plan. Determines man-hours, personnel, parts and facility requirements
to repair UAS and associated equipment. Plans maintenance areas, component repair, technical
inspection techniques, and procedures, according to directives, technical manuals, work standards, and
operational policies. Maintains supply economy and discipline. Supervises the unmanned aircraft systems
technical training program. Prepares evaluations, special reports, and records pertaining to unmanned
aircraft systems maintenance and related activities. Recommends and administers plans and policies.
     b. Physical demands rating and qualifications for initial award or reclassification of MOS.
        (1) The Tactical Unmanned Aircraft System (TUAS) Specialist must possess the following
qualifications: Waivers, and/or exceptions must be approved by CDR, AVCOE, ATTN: ATZQ-CDF-P, Ft
Rucker, AL 36362-1100, (https://home.army.mil/rucker/about/AVCOE/opfd/enlisted).
       (a) A physical demands rating of Significant (Gray).
       (b) A physical profile of 111221.
       (c) Normal color vision.
       (d) Qualifying scores.
              (1) A minimum score of 93 in aptitude area EL, 99 in aptitude area MM, and 102 in aptitude
area SC.
              (2) A minimum OPAT score of Standing Long Jump (LJ) – 0140 cm, Seated Power Throw
(PT) – 0400 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) – 0140 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) – 0040 shuttles in
Physical Demand Category “Significant” (Gray).
       (e) A U.S. Citizen.
       (f) A high school graduate or equivalent.
       (g) A security eligibility of SECRET is required prior to attendance/arrival for training, initial award of
the MOS and to maintain the MOS. An interim SECRET security access granted by CCF meets this
requirement.
       (h) Complete, pass and maintain the Army Class 4 medical physical prior to requesting and/or
granting the MOS to the Soldier and his or her attendance/arrival to training/school. Not required to
complete or pass the Type II decompression sickness/chamber training requirement.
       (i) Formal training conducted by the United States Army Aviation Center of Excellence (AVCOE) or
by AVCOE-certified instructors is mandatory to qualify for award of the MOS.
       (j) Reclassification: Must meet the above qualifications and all prerequisites IAW AR 614-200
“Reclassification of primary military occupational specialty and/or secondary military occupational
specialty” chapter and AR 40-501 “Medical Fitness Standards for Retention and Separation, including
Retirement” chapter. MOS 15X is closed to individuals in the grade SGT or above unless they have
previously held MOS 15C/E/M/W/X for a minimum of 12 months at skill level 1 or 2, 18 months at skill
level 3 or 24 months at skill level 4.
              1. Active Component: Soldiers that do not meet the above qualifications must submit a
determination packet to CDR, AVCOE, ATTN: ATZQ-CDF-P, Ft Rucker, AL 36362-1100,
(https://home.army.mil/rucker/about/AVCOE/opfd/enlisted).
              2. National Guard: Soldiers that do not meet the above qualifications must submit a waiver
packet through the National Guard Bureau, ATTN: NGB-ARNG-AV, 111 South George Mason Drive,
Arlington, VA 22204-1382 (ng.ncr.ngb-arng.mbx.avn-trng-mgtarmy.mil).
              3. Reserve Component: Soldiers that do not meet the above qualifications must submit a
waiver packet through Commander, Army Reserve Aviation Command (ARAC), ATTN: G3 (AFAK-OPT),
1160 Brandenburg Station Road, Ft Knox, KY 40121-4190, (usarmy.usarc.arac.list.g-37-
training@army.mil
       (2) MOS closed for reclassification to Soldiers who have been deemed permanently non-deployable
in accordance with AR 40-501, AR 220-1, AR 600-8-101, and AR 614-30. Soldiers must meet the
minimum criteria for retainability stated in AR 635-40, paragraph 3-5(a) and be fully deployable to all
locations and echelons.
     c. Additional skill identifiers. (Note: Refer to table 12-8 for listing of universal ASI’s associated with all
enlisted MOS.)
       (1) F8--Unmanned Aircraft Systems Master Gunner
       (2) G3--Air Cavalry Leaders Course
       (3) U7--Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) Instructor Operator (I/O)
     d. Physical requirements and standards of grade. Physical requirements and standards of grade
relating to each skill level are listed in the following tables:
       (1) Table 10-15X-1. Physical requirements.
       (2) Table 10-15X-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
       (3) Table 10-15X-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
